scenario: AITA for not jumping up and helping my parents bring in the groceries? I'm an adult and I pay rent if that helps. | I'm 33 years old and I've pretty much always lived with my parents. To me there's no shame in it because it's super cheap (they charge me $200, which honestly would be market rate where we live) and it has everything I want and need without the hassle of having to look for a new place to live. We get along most of the time but honestly I just avoid them. Recently the toilet flooded in my bathroom which means they are having to remodel my section of the house so we "run into" each other a lot more than when I used to lock myself in my room most of the time. Well today my parents went to Costco. When they got home I was sitting on the couch playing Apex and my mom asked me to get up and help them bring in groceries. I told her in a minute. I was honestly too into my game to notice that they made several trips back and forth and finally my dad told me to get my ass up. I told him I would in a minute. He said a minute is now and grabbed the controller out of my hand. It turned into a huge shouting match and now they are checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday (which is basically impossible). Of course they brought up my younger brother who is married with two kids and was just promoted at his job. They have their golden child of course but to throw his shit in my face is bullshit. I mean I guess I could have gotten up and helped them but to me because I pay rent that gives me the privilege to pretty much say no when they ask me for stuff like helping with groceries or yard work. Am I the asshole in this situation?

prediction.raw: 1. You are the asshole in this situation. While it's understandable that you want to prioritize your own activities and feel that paying rent entitles you to some autonomy, refusing to help your parents with groceries after they asked you multiple times is inconsiderate and disrespectful. Your parents are still providing you with a place to live, even if you are paying rent, and it's reasonable for them to expect some level of cooperation and assistance with household tasks. Additionally, your response to their requests, telling them "in a minute" repeatedly and then getting into a shouting match when they pressed the issue, demonstrates a lack of empathy and understanding for their perspective. It's not just about the groceries; it's about showing respect and appreciation for the people who are providing for you. Your argument that paying rent gives you the privilege to say no to helping with household tasks is flawed. Paying rent is a financial transaction, but it doesn't necessarily mean you're exempt from contributing to the household in other ways. In fact, many people who pay rent to family members or roommates still help out with chores and tasks as a way of showing appreciation and being a considerate member of the household. It's also worth noting that your parents' decision to check into a hotel and give you an ultimatum may be an overreaction, but it's clear that they feel frustrated and disrespected by your behavior. Rather than blaming them for throwing your brother's accomplishments in your face, you might want to take this opportunity to reflect on your own behavior and consider how you can be a more respectful and considerate member of your household.
